books.locked: The books are in order now. Best to leave them.
c1.ash: Ash. Cold, and very fine, like something that was a long time ago.
c1.books_look: Four books stand out from the others, each with its own colour and pattern. Their order feels wrong.
c1.books_solved: The last book slides into place. Somewhere below, a catch lets go: the cabinet door swings open.
c1.books_sorted: Red stripes, green dots, pale chevrons, plain yellow: just as in the painting.
c1.cabinet_shut: The cabinet door is shut fast. There is no keyhole. Something else holds it.
c1.candle_already: The candle is already burning. The match would only be wasted.
c1.candle_lit: The match flares. The candle takes it, grudgingly.
c1.candle_take: You lift the burning candle from its saucer, shielding the flame with your hand.
c1.candle_unlit: A candle stub on the mantel. It has never been lit, or has been lit too often.
c1.chart_take: A chart of the lake, pinned beside the window. You take it. Something in the margin makes you uneasy.
c1.clock_set: The hands stop. Something inside the case clicks, and a little hatch swings open.
c1.door_unlocked: Something clunks deep in the door. It swings open onto the jetty and the fog beyond.
c1.drawer_locked: The drawer has a brass-rimmed keyhole. Locked.
c1.drawer_open: The key turns. The drawer slides open.
c1.fish_engraving: A tiny fish is engraved on the clock face, right beside the four.
c1.food_take: A tin of fish food, labelled with a drawing of a fish. Whoever wrote the label had a sense of humour.
c1.hatch_open: The hatch hangs open, empty now.
c1.hatch_shut: A little hatch under the clock face. It doesn't budge.
c1.intro: You wake in a lakeside cottage. The lamp is out, the clock has stopped, and the goldfish is staring at you.
c1.jar_frantic: A moth beats itself against the glass of the jar, frantic. It would calm down if there were a light to look at.
c1.jar_open: You lift the lid. The moth sits very still, then rises, and the room tilts away from you.
c1.lake_shapes: Now the moth hangs over the glass, four pale shapes surface in the dark water, upside down: an eye, a moon, a fish, a bell.
c1.lake_still: The lake is perfectly still. Not a ripple. A single pinprick of light sits on the horizon, far off. It is out.
c1.lantern_burning: It burns steadily in the window. You'll take it with you when you go.
c1.lantern_lit: The candle gives up its flame. The lantern burns, small and steady.
c1.lantern_oiled: You fill the lantern. The wick drinks greedily.
c1.lantern_placed: You set the lantern in the window. Far out on the lake, a pinprick of light answers it.
c1.lantern_take: A storm lantern, cold and dry. You take it.
c1.leave: You step out onto the jetty, the lantern swinging in your hand. The door shuts behind you.
c1.leave_missing.chart: You can't leave without the chart of the lake. Something in you is certain.
c1.leave_missing.oar: You can't leave without the oar. You'll be rowing, one way or another.
c1.leave_missing.ticket: There was a ticket in the coat. Take it before you go. It's dated for a day that hasn't come.
c1.lockbox: A lock with four dials. Each one shows a different shape.
c1.mat_lift: You lift the corner of the doormat. Something is tucked beneath it: a scrap of paper.
c1.match_take: A single match, kept where only the clock could keep it.
c1.mirror.1: Your reflection nods. A moment after you do.
c1.mirror.2: It runs late again. Half a second, no more, like an echo that has to run to catch you.
c1.mirror.3: It catches up, out of breath, and holds something out to you through the glass: a corner of a photograph.
c1.mirror.4: It stands very still now. Waiting, perhaps.
c1.moth_free: The moth circles the flame, content.
c1.moth_w: The moth presses itself against the glass, drawn to the lantern.
c1.moth_window: The moth drifts to the lantern in the window and settles there, trembling in the warmth.
c1.note_take: A note, in your own handwriting, signed with a single initial: R.
c1.oar_take: A good ash oar, worn smooth at the grip. You take it.
c1.oil_take: A bottle of lamp oil. You take it.
c1.painting_dark: The painting tells you nothing. It's too dark to make out more than smears of paint.
c1.painting_lit: In the candlelight the picture swims up out of the dark: a lake, a far lighthouse, four floats in a row, a heron at the edge.
c1.painting_seen: Four floats across still water. Each one has its own colour, and its own pattern.
c1.pell_chat.1: "I'm only a fish," says Pell. "A fish who sees everything. It's not the same thing as helping."
c1.pell_chat.2: "Don't look at me. The clock is on the other wall."
c1.pell_chat.3: "It's very quiet, isn't it? The lake hasn't moved in years."
c1.pell_chat.5: "Light things. It's what we do here."
c1.pell_chat.6: Pell blows a bubble, regards it, and lets it go.
c1.pell_clock: "Both hands pointed straight at me. I was there, you know. Make of that what you will."
c1.pell_fed: Pell falls on the flakes with enormous dignity, and no dignity at all. When he's done he looks up. "Both hands pointed straight at me," he says.
c1.pell_full: Pell hasn't room for another flake. He tells you so, in bubbles.
c1.pell_hungry: The goldfish watches you with one oddly human eye, and then, pointedly, at his empty surface.
c1.photo: A photograph of this very room. Someone is standing in it, back to the camera, exactly where you are standing now.
c1.plaque: A pike, mounted on a plaque. Its glass eye holds yours a moment longer than it should.
c1.pocket_empty: Empty now. Just lint and the smell of rain.
c1.pocket_l: Your fingers find paper in the left pocket: a ferry ticket.
c1.pocket_r: In the right pocket, cold against your fingertips: a brass key.
c1.sill_unlit: A dark lantern in a window is only a lantern. It needs a flame first.
c1.sorry: Burned letters. One word survived the fire.
c1.ticket_take: A ferry ticket. Dated tomorrow. You take it, though you couldn't say why.

clock.locked: The hands are fixed now. Whatever the clock was holding has been let go.
combine.generic.1: Those two have nothing to say to each other.
combine.generic.3: You turn them over in your hands. No.
combine.key.lantern: The key and the lantern have nothing to do with each other.
combine.lantern.candle_lit: The wick drinks nothing. The lantern is dry. It needs oil before it can use your flame.
combine.oil.candle_lit: Fire and lamp oil, without a lantern in between. No.
dials.locked: The dials are set. The lock has done its work.
frag.get: A fragment of a photograph. ({0} of 10)
game.tagline: Relight the lights. Recover five memories. Find out why the lamp went out at 4:20.
game.title: Still Water
hint.1.1.2: The coat has two pockets. Try both.
hint.1.1.3: The brass key is in the right pocket.
hint.1.10.1: Now that the moth is at the window, look out at the lake.
hint.1.10.2: Four shapes in the water, upside down. The door has four dials.
hint.1.10.3: Eye, moon, fish, bell: set the dials in that order, left to right.
hint.1.2.2: Under the window: a brass-rimmed keyhole.
hint.1.2.3: Use the key on the desk drawer, under the window.
hint.1.3.1: Someone in this room is hungry.
hint.1.3.2: The tin from the drawer. The bowl is on the west wall.
hint.1.3.3: Use the fish food on the bowl, then speak to him.
hint.1.4.1: Clocks. Never trust a stopped one.
hint.1.4.2: There's something tiny engraved on that clock face. Near the four.
hint.1.4.3: Both hands on the fish. Twenty past four. Honestly.
hint.1.5.1: You got something out of that clock. Fire needs a flame.
hint.1.5.2: A candle stub on the mantel, right of the clock.
hint.1.5.3: Use the match on the candle.
hint.1.6.1: The painting tells you nothing in the dark.
hint.1.6.2: Take the burning candle. Light helps a painting.
hint.1.6.3: Pick up the lit candle and hold it to the painting.
hint.1.7.1: Four books on the shelf. Four floats in the painting.
hint.1.7.2: Put the books in the order of the floats, left to right. Match the patterns, not just the colours.
hint.1.7.3: Red stripes, green dots, pale chevrons, plain yellow. Swap them until they stand that way.
hint.1.8.1: The lantern is dry. Something in the cabinet isn't.
hint.1.8.2: Oil first, then a flame, then a window.
hint.1.8.3: Combine oil with the lantern, then the lit candle with the lantern, then use it on the windowsill.
hint.1.9.1: That moth has been banging on its jar all evening.
hint.1.9.2: It will calm down now there's a light burning.
hint.1.9.3: Open the jar on the desk.
hint.none: Nothing is stuck. Look around, then look again.
hintr.1.1.2: R. — a coat has two pockets. Check them both.
hintr.1.2.1: R. — the desk has a drawer. Under the window.
hintr.1.2.2: R. — brass-rimmed keyhole. You know the one.
hintr.1.2.3: R. — the key from the coat, in the drawer.
hintr.1.3.1: R. — you were told to feed the fish.
hintr.1.3.2: R. — the tin from the drawer; the bowl on the west wall.
hintr.1.3.3: R. — the food on the bowl. Then talk to him.
item.candle_lit.desc: A stub of candle on its saucer. The flame leans away from your breath.
item.candle_lit.name: Lit candle
item.chart.desc: A chart of the lake on a five-by-five grid. A spot is circled in red. Something is written in the margin.
item.chart.name: Chart of the lake
item.chart.text:
STERN TO HOME.
DO NOT LOOK DOWN.
item.food.desc: A tin of flakes. The label is a drawing of a very pleased fish.
item.food.name: Fish food
item.key.desc: Heavy, worn, warm from the pocket it came out of.
item.key.name: Brass key
item.lantern.desc: A storm lantern. Cold, dry, and not much use like this.
item.lantern.name: Lantern
item.lantern_lit.desc: A storm lantern, burning small and steady. You can carry the light with you.
item.lantern_lit.name: Lantern (lit)
item.lantern_oil.desc: The lantern, filled with oil. It needs a flame.
item.lantern_oil.name: Lantern (filled)
item.match.desc: A single match with a red head.
item.match.name: Match
item.note.desc: A note to yourself, in your own hand.
item.note.name: R.'s note
item.oar.desc: An ash oar, worn smooth at the grip. One of a pair, you suspect.
item.oar.name: Oar
item.oil.desc: A bottle of lamp oil, three-quarters full.
item.oil.name: Lamp oil
item.ticket.desc: A night-ferry ticket for one crossing. The date on it is tomorrow's.
item.ticket.name: Ferry ticket
item.ticket.text:
NIGHT FERRY
One crossing
Valid: tomorrow
look.armchair: An armchair by the fire. When you put your hand on the seat, it is still warm.
look.barometer: A barometer. The needle points firmly at STORMY, and has done for a long time.
look.coal: A coal scuttle. Nothing has been burned here for a long time. Nothing but paper.
look.desk: A heavy desk. Ink-stained, scarred with years of elbows.
look.generic.2: It doesn't have anything to say.
look.generic.3: You look. It looks like itself.
look.oar_stand: An umbrella stand for oars. Only the one oar left in it.
look.table: A little round table, kept for the bowl and nothing else.
look.vase: Dry reeds in a vase. They rattle when the air moves, and the air is not moving.
nb.clock_fish.text: A tiny fish is engraved on the clock face, beside the four. Pell: "Both hands pointed straight at me."
nb.clock_fish.text2: A tiny fish beside the four. Both hands pointed at it. The clock stopped at 4:20.
nb.clock_fish.title: The stopped clock
nb.floats.text: Four floats on dark water, left to right: red with stripes, green with dots, pale with chevrons, yellow and plain.
nb.floats.title: The floats
nb.shapes.text: Four shapes in the water, upside down, left to right: an eye, a moon, a fish, a bell.
nb.shapes.title: Shapes in the lake
notebook.empty: Nothing in here yet. The notebook sketches what you have seen, never what it means.
notebook.title: Keeper's notebook
notebook.updated: The notebook has a new sketch.
pause.title: Paused
satchel.full: The satchel is full. Something has to be used up first.
settings.title: Settings
title.confirm_new: Starting a new game replaces your current save. Begin again?
use.bowl.key: Pell regards the key with contempt. He's a fish, not a locksmith.
use.bowl.match: Pell recoils from the match. "Fish. Water. Do the arithmetic."
use.bowl.oil: Pell is not a lamp. He says so.
use.candle.key: The key has nothing to do with the candle.
use.clock.match: The match is for something that burns, not for something that ticks.
use.coat.key: You have already found everything the coat has to give.
use.door.key: The key was meant for something with a drawer.
use.drawer.food: Feeding a drawer. Pell would never let you hear the end of it.
use.drawer.match: A match won't open a lock.
use.generic.4: You try it. The room is unimpressed.
use.grate.candle_lit: You hold the candle to the grate. The ash is far too cold to catch.
use.jar.key: The jar doesn't want a key. It wants a reason to stay calm.
use.lantern_desk.candle_lit: It's easier to light a lantern you're holding.
use.lantern_desk.oil: It's easier to fill a lantern you're holding.
use.lockplate.key: The key was meant for something with a drawer.
use.mirror.candle_lit: The mirror shows you a candle. A moment late.
use.painting.match: A match won't last long enough to show you a whole painting.
use.painting_surface.key: You can't unlock a painting. Believe me, you want to.
use.painting_surface.match: A match won't last long enough to show you a whole painting.
use.pell.key: Pell regards the key with contempt. He's a fish, not a locksmith.
use.pell.oil: Pell is not a lamp. He says so.
use.photo.candle_lit: You hold the flame to the photograph. Nothing new comes out of the dark.
use.sill.candle_lit: A candle in a window is just a candle. A lantern in a window is a lighthouse.
use.sill.lantern: A dark lantern in a window is only a lantern. It needs oil and a flame first.
